metadata.topic: Thermal Physics — Specific Heat Capacity from Graph Gradient: c = P/(mG)
metadata.note: Uses G from PHY-JUN23-Q1d (expected 0.0875 °C/s). P=105W, m=300g=0.3kg. c = P/(mG) = 105/(0.3×0.0875) = 105/0.02625 = 4000 J/(kg·°C). To 1 s.f.: 4000 J/(kg·°C). Wide tolerance (±800) accommodates own-figure from different gradient readings. Answer matches Milk (3900 J/kg/°C) from Q1e(ii).

question.name: CSEC Phy Jun 2023 Q1e(i) — Specific Heat Capacity from c = P/(mG)
question.text:
Given that the gradient of the temperature-time graph is G, and that:

G = P / (m × c)

where P = 105 W (heater power) and m = 300 g (mass of liquid), calculate the specific heat capacity c of the liquid using your gradient from Q1(d).

Express your answer in SI units, to one significant figure. (6 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Model solution (using G = 0.0875 °C/s):
Rearrange: G = P/(mc) → c = P/(mG)
Convert mass: m = 300 g = 0.3 kg
c = 105 / (0.3 × 0.0875) = 105 / 0.02625 = 4000 J/(kg·°C)
To 1 s.f.: c = 4000 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹

Own-figure marking: CSEC awards full marks if the correct formula and mass conversion are used with the student's own G value. Comparing with Table 2: c ≈ 4000 J/kg/°C matches Milk (3900 J/kg/°C) most closely.

steps.label:
Given: P = 105 W  |  m = 300 g  |  G = gradient from Q1(d) ≈ 0.0875 °C/s
Formula: G = P/(mc) → rearrange to c = P/(mG)
Unit conversion: 1 kg = 1000 g  |  SI unit for c: J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹
Convert mass and set up the formula for c. (2 marks)
Calculate c = P/(mG) and express to one significant figure. (4 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Convert grams to kilograms: m = 300 ÷ 1000 = 0.3 kg. SI units require kg.
Multiply m (in kg) by G (in °C/s): 0.3 × 0.0875 = 0.02625. Use your own gradient if different.

fields.label: c = P / (m × G) = _____ J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹
fields.diagnostic_hint: c = P/(mG) = 105/0.02625 = 4000 J/(kg·°C). Divide heater power by (mass × gradient).

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Rearrange G = P/(mc): multiply both sides by c, then divide by G → c = P/(mG).

fields.label: c to 1 significant figure = _____ J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹
fields.diagnostic_hint: 4000 is already expressed to 1 significant figure (the leading 4 is the single significant figure)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Round to 1 significant figure: the first non-zero digit counts as 1 s.f. 4000 J/(kg·°C) has 1 s.f. (only the '4' is significant here).
